items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: But he played in orchestra with Piron.

ctx.x: So Old Man Contrell was in there too, huh?

Oh yeah, he was a great drummer, one of your greatest drummers. But he played in orchestra with Piron. Well you see at those times that's how guys would play with two bands. Some guys didn't have a brass band but they had orchestra and they took practically to Goodman's for parades.
So your Uncle Clay now, did he play anything but street drums?

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: Well, their band sounded, the orchestra, like old Pierron band.

ctx.x: Can you remember what any of the dance bands were like up there when you were, oh, as far back as you can remember? That is, did it sound like the New Orleans jazz bands here? Was it a different type of music? What would you say? How did it compare?
Well, their band sounded, the orchestra, like old Pierron band.
Oh, yes. Yeah. They made a few records, so we have an idea about how that sounded.
